articles.title: ‘I was mesmerised by how the fog turned the tower into a monolith’: Derek Zhao’s best phone picture
articles.summary: Zhao was out jogging around Treasure Island, near San Francisco, when he spotted a lonely tower stabbing through the clouds. Every morning, Derek Zhao jogs the perimeter of Treasure Island, his home, situated an eight-minute ferry ride from San Francisco.
body: Zhao works as a machine-learning engineer at Disney California. He relocated from Texas last year to take up the role, finding the 400-acre human-made island to be the perfect location, “close enough to the office and all the culture the city has to offer, but far enough that I’m waking up to the sound of seagulls instead of car horns”.

He took this image earlier this year, stopping mid-jog to capture the top of San Francisco’s Salesforce Tower. “I was mesmerised by how the fog, caused by what’s known as a marine layer, completely covered the rest of the skyline, leaving only the tower looking like a monolith,” he says. “It’s ironic that something that obscures, like fog, can make a scene more clear.”

It’s only recently that Zhao has come to realise that his favourite photos don’t come from travels with his professional cameras, but “improbable scenes near home that somehow only reveal themselves when I’m not expecting them. It brings me considerable peace that despite living in such close proximity to the centre of things I feel ambivalent about – tech, AI, urban density, hustle culture – the universe can still grant such awe-inspiring moments of quiet.

articles.title: How Athens discovered a new, confident Greek cuisine
articles.summary: Athens is now a food capital where you can enjoy bustling bars, traditional taverna fare or unearth a new-wave gem in its many restaurants – but it wasn’t always this way See our recommendations for eating and drinking around Athens.
body: Visiting Athens for its food might have sounded like a joke to previous generations. Unlike many other Mediterranean countries, including Italy, Spain and Turkey, Greece had no renaissance and no aristocracy to fund chefs and develop sophisticated cuisines. Simple village dishes didn’t always translate well: in the past, tourists would suffer a summer scorching and some desiccated moussaka so they could puff up the Acropolis in August before skedaddling to an island. However, recently the Greek capital has undergone a gastronomic renaissance.

In the 1980s, Athenians were leaving behind a history of rural poverty, fasoláda bean stew, and a largely vegetarian diet. They discovered fast food and began eating too much meat. The 1990s saw new levels of wealth; brunch, sushi and lobster spaghetti were aspirational goals for the upwardly mobile. By the time of the 2004 Athens Olympics, a cohort of Athenians existed who had never known hunger, war or dictatorship. Consequently, the economic crisis that began in 2009 was a devastating shock and the next decade saw severe unemployment and deprivation, accompanied by an influx of traumatised refugees and migrants.

articles.title: Cooking with Tom Kerridge, the Michelin ‘meatfluencer’
articles.summary: The star chef demystified the restaurant scene with his love of a welcoming pub. Now he explains why hospitality is in crisis – and how to make a sublime venison chilli.
body: Tom Kerridge is the king of meat: first as a chef, transforming pub classics like pork belly into Michelin-starred fare at The Hand and Flowers in Marlow 20 years ago, and later opening The Butcher’s Tap and Grill in the same village; then as a cookery writer: his Outdoor Cooking – The Ultimate Modern Barbecue Bible of 2021 is well named, being both as comprehensive and as worshipful as a holy book; and recently as a “meat-fluencer”, making gorgeous skills videos on Instagram and YouTube.

That was just destiny, he says (more or less). “When you’re cooking in a classic brigade system, the sections are like a larder: you’ve got starters, you’ve got garnish, you’ve got meat and fish, you’ve got pastry. The meat is the lead section, where the most experienced chef is, because that’s where you land when you’ve learned to treat vegetables with love and respect. If you fuck up cabbage, it doesn’t cost a lot.” It’s true, it doesn’t, but if you saw the care Kerridge puts into dicing an onion – peeling its layers apart like he’s making a mosaic, assiduous even about half an inch of waste – of an onion – you’d know that love and respect aren’t really about money.

articles.title: The Pillowy-Soft Caraa Duffel Is My Ultimate Road Trip Bag
articles.summary: Here's why I schlep the Caraa duffel bag with me practically everywhere I go.
body: I’m always looking for a good excuse to get out of town for the weekend, and more often than not, that means jumping in the car. From my little Brooklyn, New York abode, that generally means heading out east for beachy trips to Montauk, hopping around upstate’s Hudson Valley or Catskills towns, and taking advantage of ski mountains all over the east coast. These are the road trips I take again and again, and for almost two years, the Caraa Portobello duffel has been my go-to bag for every single one of them.

I have the duffel bag in olive, a timeless, earthy shade of green that looks great with the rest of my luggage. I love its looks, but what has really kept it in my rotation is how well it suits the way I actually pack. The Portobello is pillowy-soft, and the shoulder straps are long enough to sit comfortably over my arm—an underrated quality that really matters when I’m pulling it out of the car trunk, carrying it into a hotel, or hauling it around for the day. I also love the button clasp that brings the straps together. A small detail, true—but one that makes the bag feel particularly easy to grab, sling over my shoulder, and go.

articles.title: 7 Fall Outfit Ideas Where the Skirt Is the Look
articles.summary: The spring 2027 runways—Prada’s, in particular—continue to champion the skirt in all its forms. Here’s how to style a skirt for right now.
body: For its spring 2027 fashion show on Tuesday, Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons presented a collection dedicated entirely to skirts. Vogue’s Nicole Phelps declared it a “people pleaser from start to finish, direct and designed to stoke real world desire.” A rave. Many in the industry echoed her sentiment.

Mrs. Prada’s love for skirts is well-documented. “The skirt for me is like a T-shirt,” she said in a 2006 interview with Charlie Rose. Fan accounts dedicated to the designer’s personal style have documented her wearing skirts almost exclusively: with sweaters, shirts, and cropped boxy jackets; with kitten heels and loafers—and with Prada-eccentric accessories. It’s proof that the skirt, for all of its supposedly fussy and femme connotations, can be a real wardrobe workhorse, able to infuse a look with personality without pushing it over the top. “It can be… eccentric,” Prada said in the same interview, “but it doesn’t change you as much because it’s waist down.”
points: The spring 2027 runways—Prada’s, in particular—continue to champion the skirt in all its forms.

articles.title: Demi Moore and Tallulah Willis Do Mother-Daughter Dressing in Summery Suiting
articles.summary: The pair coordinated in Thom Browne skirt suits, making a persuasive case for keeping summer dressing going a little longer.
body: Like mother, like daughter—at least when it comes to end-of-summer-tailoring. Yesterday, Demi Moore and Tallulah Willis arrived at Step Up’s 2026 Annual Inspiration Awards at the Skirball Cultural Center in coordinating Thom Browne skirt suits, putting a distinctly preppy spin on mother-daughter dressing.

Moore’s Nantucket-print suit was the more whimsical of the two, covered in a beachy illustrated scene that ekes out the last few drops of summer. The set comprised a tailored blazer and pleated, step-hem knee-length skirt, worn with a sky-blue shirt and coordinating striped tie. She leaned fully into the designer’s school uniform-y codes with white tube socks and pointed blue-and-white T-bar pumps, finishing the look with a structured white leather handbag and square-framed glasses. Her signature raven hair was back to almost hip-skimming length. The actor was among Step Up’s honorees.

Willis followed her mother’s lead in a dove-gray Thom Browne skirt suit accented with red-and-white striping. With her hair cut into a tousled lob and a pair of oval sunglasses perched on her face, her take felt a little more relaxed.
points: The pair coordinated in Thom Browne skirt suits, making a persuasive case for keeping summer dressing going a little longer.

articles.title: Behind Edward Buchanan’s Hub for Black Creatives
articles.summary: The industry legend has opened a new center to house and foster under-represented talent. And he’s done it without a hint of outside investment.
body: For Ohio-born designer Edward Buchanan, Black industry mentors changed his life. While finishing his studies at New York’s Parsons School of Design, designer Gordon Henderson put him forward for interviews at major fashion houses, while Rodney Patterson gave him a tip off about an opening at Bottega Veneta, where he would become the first ready-to-wear design director. Now, more than three decades on, the creative director and knitwear specialist has opened a self-funded foundation to continue that lineage.

The result is a 400-square-meter building located in NoLo — a historically working-class and multicultural district of Milan — dedicated to fostering and guiding creative talents from under-represented communities, including people of color (POC), queer, and female cultural practitioners. Crucially, Buchanan will ensure the non-profit remains financially autonomous, with no outside investment. He’s calling it The Situation, after the design consultancy he co-founded in 2012.
